registryBinding.rule: each keys[] row must equal its declaration: kind, placeholder names in declared order with the declared slot type, and resultLimitBytes for a format (absent for text); the declarations, not this document, own those facts

retiredKeys.rule: semantic keys deliberately removed from the declarations: each a valid key, listed once in ascending order, never an active declaration. No current key is retired. keySchema.shape: two or more dot-separated segments of lower-case ASCII letters, digits and _, each segment starting with a letter

textContract.encoding: well-formed UTF-8: the shortest-form encoding of Unicode scalar values only

textContract.acceptanceProves: no native glyph, font, locale or visibility behavior

staticText: shown exactly as stored; never formatted

Sent does not prove that another player stored it.

keys.english: Local roll record: Nexus records its rolling decisions automatically, on this computer only. It keeps Echo ids, the offers, charges, the action chosen and sent, and the result seen. Owned and locked counts are kept for your Wishlist targets only, not for all your Echoes. It keeps no account, character, realm or Wishlist name, no chat and no credential, and it sends nothing anywhere.

Keep every /nexus command, option word (on, off, adaptive, released ...), quoted on-screen label and the names Nexus, EchoWeaver and Project Ebonhold exactly as written; translate the surrounding sentences. Button and window names in the text (Plan, Explore, Build Library, Options, Auto ON/OFF, Sync Now ...) should match how those labels are translated in their own windows. Game terms (Echo, Wishlist, Saved Build, Orb, Take, Banish, Reroll, Freeze, Lost Memories) follow the game client's wording. keys.english: Continue with an unconfirmed Orb outcome? The earlier Orb action counts {spent} of its approved {limit} Orb(s) as spent. Nexus did not see which Echo, if any, you received, and the game gives no way to check. If you continue: the spent count stays; the original record is saved unchanged; nothing is refunded, repeated or chosen; Nexus stops blocking rolling; a new Orb run needs its own approval and every normal check. Risk you accept: Nexus cannot prove that the server is finished with the old action. Two answers that arrived after Nexus asked do not prove that no older answer is still on its way. A late result would show up as an ordinary change, and Nexus will not link it to the old record.
